coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel D
record.summary: Phase 1 residential parcel between Building 2 and the new 21st Street, 90 ft under the D4D, designed by Stanley Saitowitz | Natoma Architects as an L-shaped building of seven residential levels over ground-floor retail with loft townhouses along 21st Street. It has not started construction; the Port's proposed 2026 amendments would require closing on it by 2029-2030.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. Street-facing edge re-clipped 2026-09-17 against official curb-referenced street data -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Residential (studio-3BR over 7 levels) + ground-floor retail + townhouses along 21st St, designed by Stanley Saitowitz/Natoma Architects. A weak secondary source implied a ~2020 completion, but this directly conflicts with Brookfield's own July 2026 statement that its first market-rate residential building at Pier 70 won't break ground until 2027 -- treat as NOT yet built.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Unit count, square footage and the date of the Saitowitz design are not stated on the architect's page and no Planning vertical design approval for Parcel D is listed on the Planning Department's Pier 70 page.
A secondary source implying a ~2020 completion is recorded in this parcel's geometry file; every primary source says no Phase 1 vertical building other than Building 12 has been built.
